cosmic-ray catalysis of false-vacuum bubble nucleation is a viable alternative to spontaneous nucleation in the context of particle physics models, but it cannot be the dominant process for phenomenological reasons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Landau-WKB approximation for catalysed decay, which is often used to calculate the decay rate, can lead to significant errors when applied to thin-walled bubbles.

, in order to obtain a cosmologically significant decay rate, perturbative models must produce thick-walled false-vacuum bubbles, which will always decay via quantum tunelling, regardless of any cosmic-ray catalysis.
